date: Approx. 30-35 H (650-656); his killing: Dhu al-Hijja 35 H (June 656)
title: 11zh5hi
The Era of Caliph Uthman, the Siege of Medina and Imam Ali
hook: As complaints grew, Imam Ali mediated in Medina. Afterwards, the pledge of allegiance was demanded of him.
scenes.0.text: Caliph Uthman's first years in Medina passed calmly. In the second half, governorships and wealth became a subject of complaint. In particular, the **Umayyads** were appointed to important posts. The TDV article on Uthman records Walid b. Uqba and then Sa'id b. al-As for Kufa, Abdullah b. Sa'd for Egypt, Abdullah b. Amir for Basra, and Marwan for the secretariat. It also records that he made **Mu'awiya** governor-general of Syria and enlarged his authority with Homs, Qinnasrin and Palestine. The first appointment in Damascus predates him, in Umar's time. Favoritism is putting relatives into office. The treasury is the common property of the Ummah. It was complained that most of the spoils were allotted to relatives and that large gifts were given to governors. Imam Ali also criticized this. The earlier shura, that is, consultative council, had set aside **Imam Ali**'s right. Now offices and wealth were gathered in the hands of this family. On the day of the siege, Uthman would recall a promise the Prophet had given.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.1.text: Delegations came to Medina from Egypt, Kufa and Basra. The complaint rested on the Umayyad appointments and the use of the common treasury called the bayt al-mal. The people of Medina heard these objections at close quarters. **Imam Ali** had not yet intervened. It would fall to him to warn Uthman.
scenes.2.text: **Imam Ali** warned Caliph Uthman in Medina. He conveyed the people's complaint and asked that his conduct change. When the Egyptian delegation drew near, at Uthman's request Imam Ali and Muhammad b. Maslama spoke with them. With the promise that the complaints would be redressed, the delegation returned. Imam Ali stood between the two sides so that no blood would be shed.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.3.text: The agreement broke down. **Imam Ali** said that Marwan would put Uthman in difficulty and advised him to keep away from him. A letter is also mentioned. Who wrote the letter is debated. The advice was not heeded. The matter reached a siege in Medina.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.3.art.actors.2.label: sbbh7k
Marwan
scenes.4.text: The siege began in Medina. Caliph Uthman withdrew into his house. Water and food became scarce. Uthman said, "The Prophet took a pledge from me, and I am bearing it with patience." **Imam Ali**, for his part, still wanted the bloodshed to stop.
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.5.text: While the siege continued, according to the narration, **Imam Ali** sent **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn** to guard Uthman's house. It is related that he also tried to get water to him. It is also said that Imam Hasan was wounded. Imam Ali, whose right had been proclaimed at Ghadir, still did not want Uthman's blood.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.5.art.actors.2.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.art.actors.3.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.6.text: Caliph Uthman was killed in Medina in Dhu al-Hijja 35 H. He was killed on 18 Dhu al-Hijja 35. His caliphate had lasted about twelve years. **Imam Ali** says in his sermon: had he given the order to kill him, he would be counted a killer. Had he held people back from him, he would have been his helper. He leaves the judgment to God. Imam Ali did not use a sword in this killing. Nor did he side with this bloodshed.
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: After Uthman, Medina was left without government for a time. The people ran to **Imam Ali** in the Prophet's Mosque. He took on this heavy responsibility knowingly. Bay'a is a pledge of allegiance. The bay'a was taken there. The state he inherited was in distress. There remained the errors, injustices, nepotism, unjustly distributed properties and corrupt governors left from the era of the caliphs before him. His first task was to establish justice. He began to take unjustly distributed properties back to the bayt al-mal and to dismiss corrupt governors. This resolve for justice would give rise to the opposition at the Camel and Siffin. The hearts of Talha and Zubayr would not fully rest in this pledge.

Talha

Imam Ali
sunni.0.says: Caliph Uthman on the day of the siege: "The Messenger of God took a pledge from me, and I am bearing it with patience."
sunni.0.grade: Tirmidhi: hasan sahih; Albani and Ali al-Za'i: sahih (Sufyan b. Waki' in the chain is weak, there is a supporting narration)
sunni.1.says: Caliph Uthman is given the glad tidings of Paradise in return for a calamity that will befall him.
sunni.2.says: The delegations, the siege and his killing are narrated in detail.
sunni.3.says: Imam Hasan's wounding and Imam Ali's stance are included in this account.
sunni.4.says: Caliph Uthman's caliphate, the delegations and the siege.
sunni.5.says: The narration that Imam Ali assigned Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn to guard Caliph Uthman's house.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali: had I given the order I would be a killer, had I prevented it I would be a helper; the judgment is God's. The number was seen in a secondary source; the text should be checked against the primary manuscript.
shia.1.says: Imam Ali describes how his right was brushed aside in the period before him.
shia.2.says: The Shia account of the events before the Camel.
shia.3.says: Relates narrations about the killing of Caliph Uthman.
shia.4.says: The matter of Caliph Uthman's blood and the correspondence between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya.
shia.5.says: Views that find the narration weak because of problems in the chain are relayed.
disputes.0.title: f08mf2
Were Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn at the house?
disputes.0.sunni: The narration of guarding and Imam Hasan's wounding are mentioned in some Sunni books (Baladhuri, Ansab al-Ashraf; Ibn Kathir, al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya). In the Sunni reading, it is also noted that Imam Ali had no control over the rebels.
disputes.0.shia: The narration of guarding is also mentioned in Baladhuri. Some Shia scholars find the chain weak; that Imam Ali did not support the siege, and the extent of his help to Caliph Uthman, are also separately discussed.
disputes.1.title: o63fch
Imam Ali's stance
disputes.1.sunni: Imam Ali warned Caliph Uthman and mediated so that the strife would not grow. The judgment of those involved in this matter later became a subject of debate.
disputes.1.shia: Imam Ali conveyed the complaints and mediated. In the Shia reading, he saw them as justified, did not approve of the shedding of blood, and left the judgment to God.
questions.0: Imam Ali both conveyed the complaint and tried to turn the delegation back. What do you think his standing in this middle ground says about the measured stance of the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: Caliph Uthman said, "The Prophet took a pledge from me, and I am bearing it with patience." How does this patience help one read those days more calmly?
questions.2: Imam Ali says he neither gave the order nor fully prevented it, and leaves the judgment to God. What does this saying teach a heart that loves him?
questions.3: The narration that Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn were at the house is regarded as weak by some scholars. How do we read such a narration with love and caution?
questions.4: Imam Ali took on the caliphate knowingly. How does his beginning to correct unjust properties and corrupt governors describe to you the love felt for him?
summary: The complaints in the second half of Caliph Uthman's reign led to the siege and his killing in 35 H. Imam Ali mediated. Uthman said, "The Prophet took a pledge from me, and I am bearing it with patience." When the people ran to him, Imam Ali took on the caliphate knowingly and began to establish justice.
key: The era of the third caliph and growing unrest
notes.0: Caliph Uthman's first years passed calmly; in the second half, governorships and the distribution of wealth became a subject of complaint.
notes.1: Delegations came to Medina from Egypt, Kufa and Basra with complaints.
notes.3: Medina was besieged and Caliph Uthman was killed in Dhu al-Hijja 35 H.
notes.4: Afterwards the people came to Imam Ali and asked him to accept their pledge of allegiance.
